issues.body: `_index_scopes` still publishes every syntactic `global` or `nonlocal` assignment from a nested function into its receiver regardless of whether that function is called, or whether it is called only after the relevant `def` executes. `_publish_into` then pins that invented launcher so an inert receiver-side rebinding cannot clear it. Also, `_scan_scope` computes `nested_view` from class-body events and passes it recursively into methods; Python method bodies do not lexically close over their class namespace. Consequently the prior executable negatives—an uncalled global publisher, a publisher called only after the default is created, and a method-local nested default sharing a class attribute name—are still falsely reported. The added negatives cover ordinary ordering and sibling scopes, but none exercises these three paths.
issues.fix_hint: Model publication at executable call/statement sites rather than hoisting declarations from arbitrary function bodies, and resolve `nonlocal` to the nearest actual enclosing function binding. When entering a class, use class locals for defaults evaluated by `def` statements in the class body, but scan method bodies against their true lexical enclosing scope rather than the class table. Add independent executable negative fixtures for the uncalled global publisher, the publisher called after default creation, and the nested method default with a same-named class attribute; assert both no findings and the runtime-captured inert value.
issues.title: Scope resolution still invents launcher bindings that defaults cannot observe

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 binding-semantics defect remains. The implementation still hoists syntactic `global`/`nonlocal` writes from nested functions without proving that those functions execute before the examined default, and it still passes a class-derived `nested_view` into method bodies even though methods do not lexically close over the class namespace. Round 5 adds many tests, but not the three executable negative cases previously requested, so those false positives remain unconstrained. This is materially the same major finding at the same severity; progress is stagnant.
